newsitem.title: USA: Hertz profits more than double to record level.
newsitem.headline: Hertz profits more than double to record level.

text.p: Hertz Corp., the car rental unit of Ford Motor Co., Thursday posted record profits of $19.7 million in the first quarter of 1997, more than double the $8.8 million it earned in the same period last year.
The increase was primarily due to higher revenues in its U.S. car rental operations, it said.
The company, the largest car rental business in the world, also achieved record revenues of $878.4 million in the first quarter, up $75.3 million from the same period last year.
It said revenues from its car rental operations were $758.5 million, up by $67.8 million, as the number of transactions and revenue per transaction increased, mainly in the U.S. market.

Revenues from its other business, industrial and construction equipment rental, increased by $13.3 million to $90.4 million, as a result of opening new locations and increased activity in industrial markets, it said.

Revenues from all other sources dropped by $5.8 million to $29.5 million due to lower revenues in its claim administration service operations, most of which were sold in February 1996. It noted that the decline was partly offset by revenues contributed by an acquisition of a foreign licensee operation in June 1996.

The company said its higher net earnings were offset by an $800,000 charge for the interest expense, net of taxes, relating to funding a $460 million dividend paid by the company to Ford in the first quarter and other items relating to the company's potential initial public offering of stock.
